clue.text: Puts down a force during exercise to avoid risk

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits within its span, so these words go inside another piece

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
lays means puts down, as in lays a carpet
taken as written
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant orders troops to lie down during training so nobody gets hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts down' and 'force' read as a military scene, but they are wordplay pieces; PE is the school abbreviation for physical education.
explanation.definitionFit: To play safe is an idiom for taking the cautious course and avoiding any risk.

clue.text: Column I covered in pargeting

indicators.note: what is covered in a coating is surrounded by it, so the coating word wraps round the single letter

parts.note: pargeting is decorative plasterwork on a wall
taken as written

explanation.surface: An architectural column covered in ornamental plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Pargeting is the raised plaster decoration seen on old houses in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilaster is a flat rectangular column set into a wall, so it is a kind of column.

clue.text: Jargon central to photography in one way?

indicators.note: the questioning 'one way' hints at a single direction of travel, here the backward one, up the column
the central part of a word is its middle, so the letters are lifted from inside that word

parts.note: the middle stretch of the word photography

explanation.surface: Specialist jargon might be central to photography, in a way.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the middle of photography from right to left; 'one way' is the backward direction in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the private vocabulary of a group, which is what jargon means.

clue.text: Bond perhaps needs cover for official crackdown

parts.note: a bond is one kind of financial security
a blanket is a cover for a bed

explanation.surface: James Bond needs a cover story for a government clampdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007, but here it is a financial instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A security blanket is an official ban on releasing information, a clampdown imposed for safety reasons.

clue.text: Get upset after month's hot

parts.note: Feb is the abbreviation for February
to rile is to annoy or upset

explanation.surface: Someone gets annoyed after a month of hot weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the month first.
explanation.definitionFit: Febrile means feverish, and someone with a fever is hot.

clue.text: A pig died being transported?

parts.note: taken as written
a boar is a male pig
d. is the abbreviation for died in records

explanation.surface: A pig died while being moved, as in a livestock lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as loose: someone aboard a vehicle is being carried along.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers aboard a ship or train are on it and so are being carried somewhere.

clue.text: See bad bank draft ruined guest house

indicators.note: something ruined has been wrecked out of its first form, so the words are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A dud bank draft has ruined a small hotel's finances.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed and breakfast is a small lodging offering a room and morning meal, essentially a guest house.

clue.text: Amazed, getting a point before scrum

parts.note: taken as written
west is a point of the compass
a ruck is a loose scrum in rugby

explanation.surface: A rugby fan is amazed when a try is scored before a scrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' suggests a score in rugby, but it is a compass point; a ruck is a loose scrum in rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Awestruck means filled with wonder, overwhelmed with astonishment.

clue.text: Uncover American guy carrying English name

indicators.note: someone carrying a load holds it within their arms, so one piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: dude is American slang for a man
E is the abbreviation for English
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An American man carries an English name tag and reveals himself.
explanation.definitionFit: To denude is to strip bare, so it means to uncover.

clue.text: Lots sleep on ends of nails

parts.note: to doze is to sleep lightly

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its two extremities, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of nails

explanation.surface: A fakir naps for long stretches on a bed of nails.
explanation.definitionFit: Dozens is used informally to mean a great many, lots.

clue.text: Rigorous working out I run over in large chapter

indicators.note: placing something in another thing puts it between that thing's edges

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
taken as written

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the preceding words are read from right to left

parts.note: to go is to run, as an engine does
C is an abbreviation for chapter

explanation.surface: A writer works out a run of argument in a long chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run over' looks like one phrase, but 'run' gives the letters and 'over' turns them, along with I, backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is strict, step-by-step reasoning, the rigorous way of working something out.

clue.text: Vegetarian food — way to live during embargo

indicators.note: something during a period falls inside its timespan, so these pieces sit within the last word

parts.note: an embargo is a ban on trade
a road is a way
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A vegetarian wonders what food is permitted while a trade embargo is in force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vegetarian food' looks like a dish description, but the definition is simply a vegetable that vegetarians eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The broad bean is a vegetable, so it is food a vegetarian eats.

clue.text: A reversal in function makes us gloomy

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, between its outer letters

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
taken as written
a turn, as in a turnaround, is a reversal

explanation.surface: A setback in some function or other leaves us feeling glum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversal' looks like an instruction to turn letters back, but here it is simply a synonym clued plainly; 'function' is the trigonometry kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine describes a sullen, gloomy temperament, once blamed on the planet Saturn's influence.

clue.text: Distinguished academic receiving alien back

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the combined letters are read leftwards
one who receives a visitor takes them in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A noted professor welcomes back a visitor from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: DON takes in ET to make DETON, which is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means well known or eminent, which is what distinguished means of a person.

clue.text: Travelling elite carrying National Trust permit

indicators.note: a traveller carrying something holds it within, so the rearranged letters hold the abbreviation
travelling elite are on the move, so their letters move about too

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
NT is the usual abbreviation for the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: Well-off travellers carry National Trust membership cards that let them into stately homes.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is the British charity that runs stately homes, so its membership card does literally permit entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle someone is to give them a right, so it is a verb meaning to permit or authorise.

clue.text: Feel feathers could be alight

definitions.note: verb phrase for a noun; read as 'what alighting could be'

parts.note: to touch is to feel
down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: Feeling feathers that might catch fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alight' suggests burning, but it means coming down to land, as a bird or plane does.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchdown is the landing of an aircraft, and to alight is to land.

clue.text: Warship expected to conquer

parts.note: a sub, or submarine, is a warship
due means expected, as a train is due

explanation.surface: A warship is expected to win the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: To subdue is to overcome and bring under control, which is to conquer.

clue.text: Something made café tart peculiar

indicators.note: peculiar means odd or strange, so the letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written, accent dropped

explanation.surface: A baker's odd creation: a peculiar café tart.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is an object made by human hands, as opposed to a natural thing.

clue.text: Left brown furniture items in store

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
umber is a brown earth pigment

explanation.surface: Brown furniture left behind in a storeroom.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain lumber means old unwanted furniture and junk put away out of use, not timber as in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumber in British use is disused furniture and odds and ends stored away, as in a lumber room.

clue.text: Win back concerning company before period of success

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
Co is the abbreviation for company
an up, as in ups and downs, is a good spell

explanation.surface: A business hopes to regain its losses ahead of a boom.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup is to recover money lost or spent, getting it back.

clue.text: Tweeter, perhaps one MP's must heed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a loudspeaker, of which a tweeter is the small high-pitched kind
second meaning: the presiding officer of the House of Commons, who keeps MPs in order

explanation.surface: Someone posting on social media whom politicians must pay attention to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweeter' suggests a social media user, but it is the hi-fi unit for treble. MP is a Member of Parliament, chaired by the Speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweeter is one example of a loudspeaker, and the Commons chair is officially titled Speaker.

clue.text: Flying latest hot type of military plane

indicators.note: flying letters are scattered through the air and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: The newest jet in the air is a hot military plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth aircraft, like the stealth bomber, are a class of warplane built to evade radar.

clue.text: Means of calculating account in a computer system

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, between its outer letters

parts.note: a bus is a data channel in a computer
a/c is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A way of doing sums: the account held on a computer system.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads on wires used for doing arithmetic.

clue.text: Czech region banning motorway drink

indicators.note: banning something keeps it out, so those letters are excluded from the region's name

parts.note: Bohemia is the western region of the Czech Republic
the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written here as MI

explanation.surface: A Czech region bans a certain drink on its motorways.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 runs London to Leeds; crosswords read its 1 as the letter I. Bohea is an old name for a black China tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohea is a kind of black tea, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Tea after test game's ending

parts.note: to check is to test
maté is a South American herbal tea

explanation.surface: Tea is served after a test match finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the tea second. 'Test' and 'game' suggest cricket, but the game is chess.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkmate is the position that ends a chess game, the king being trapped.

clue.text: Oh, no! Overturned mercury runs all around initially

indicators.note: overturned means flipped upside down, which in a down clue reads the letters bottom to top

parts.note: Hg is the chemical symbol for mercury
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letters of those words are taken

parts.note: the first letters of all and around

explanation.surface: A cry of dismay as a thermometer tips over and mercury runs everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole string, not just the mercury, is turned back in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Aargh is an exclamation of frustration or dismay, much like crying out in despair.

clue.text: Overflowing with Cape wine almost entirely

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word falls one letter short of complete

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
hock is German white wine
fully means entirely

explanation.surface: A glass brimming with South African wine from the Cape, nearly to the rim.
explanation.walkthrough: FULLY loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Chock-full means filled to capacity, packed so tight it is close to overflowing.

clue.text: Most of tax is on a gold vessel

indicators.note: most of something is all but a little, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
or is the heraldic word for gold
taken as written, to be cut short

explanation.surface: Most of the tax is charged on a golden ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a blood vessel; or is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery of the body, and an artery is a blood vessel.

clue.text: Speak about fool's ability to think straight

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to say is to speak
a nit is a fool, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: Talk about a fool's lack of clear thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanity is soundness of mind, the capacity to reason clearly and rationally.

clue.text: Note bird and rabbit

parts.note: a chit is a short note
a chat is a small songbird such as the stonechat

explanation.surface: A note listing a bird and a rabbit, like a naturalist's record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' looks like an animal but is British slang for talk, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit on is British slang for chattering idly, which is what chitchat means.
